intro: Pakistan's economy rests on farming, textiles and money sent home by workers abroad, with many people working in the informal economy.

chapters.title: Farms and textiles
text: Cotton, wheat, rice and sugar cane grow on the irrigated plains. Cotton feeds a large textile industry, which makes towels, bedsheets, jeans and clothing for the world.
Sialkot is famous for making footballs; many World Cup balls have been stitched there.

chapters.title: Challenges
text: Pakistan has often needed loans from the IMF, and rising prices have been a problem. China has invested heavily in roads, power stations and the port of Gwadar through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.

keyTerms.meaning: Money sent home by people working abroad.
The International Monetary Fund, which lends to countries in trouble.
